data.detailed_description: Chulanoor Peafowl Sanctuary, spanning 3.42 sq km of dry deciduous forests, offers an ideal peafowl habitat. Witness mesmerizing peacock courtship dances, best seen early mornings or late afternoons. This biodiverse haven also shelters Grey Partridges, Spotted Doves, Indian Robins, Green Bee-eaters, White-browed Bulbuls, along with small mammals like hares and mongooses, and various reptiles. Post-monsoon, the sanctuary bursts with butterflies, enriching its natural charm. Facilities include a visitor center, observation points, and nature trails; carry your own snacks and water. Easily accessible by road, the sanctuary is near Palakkad Junction railway station and Coimbatore International Airport. For a responsible visit, wear comfortable shoes, bring binoculars and a camera, and respect wildlife by not feeding birds, maintaining silence, and avoiding litter. Immerse yourself in this tranquil sanctuary and experience the Indian Peafowl's unparalleled beauty, a testament to Kerala's conservation efforts.
data.description:
Chulanoor Peafowl Sanctuary: Where the Peacocks Dance
Nestled amidst the serene landscapes of Palakkad district in Kerala, the Chulanoor Peafowl Sanctuary, locally known as "Mayiladumpara" (the rock where peacocks dance), is a captivating haven for India's national bird. This unique sanctuary, established in 2007 and dedicated to the memory of renowned ornithologist K.K. Neelakantan, offers an unparalleled opportunity to witness the majestic Indian Peafowl in its natural habitat.......
Spread across approximately 3.42 square kilometers of dry deciduous forests and scrubland, Chulanoor provides an ideal environment for peafowls to thrive. Early mornings and late afternoons are the best times to visit, when the male peacocks often display their spectacular iridescent plumage and perform their elaborate courtship dances – a truly mesmerizing sight for photographers and nature enthusiasts alike.
